section_summary: The section opens with the end of USAMGIK Public Health Order No. 3 (24 June 1947) on narcotics control in South Korea. It then holds the UN questionnaire on opium poppy and raw opium control, with Japanese statistical tables and SCAP's 17 July 1947 reply. The reply is followed by the South Korean reply, the Japanese Ministry of Welfare and Finance ordinances of 19 June 1946, and a second blank questionnaire with tables. The rest is State Department correspondence of August to December 1947 about sending the replies to the UN and the Permanent Central Opium Board, the board's acknowledgments, and SCAP's report of no narcotics imports or exports in the third quarter of 1947.

subfiles.about: Concluding paragraphs 12-26 of the Korean military government's narcotics regulation, from license suspension to penalties and effective date.
subfiles.from: Lee Yong Sul, Department of Public Health and Welfare, USAMGIK
subfiles.summary: Official Gazette text of paragraphs 12-26. Covers license suspension and revocation, packaging, quota permits, stamps, order forms, reports, prescriptions, record retention, storage, inspection, definitions, penalties and effective date. Signed by Lee Yong Sul by direction of the Military Governor.
subfiles.title: USAMGIK Public Health Order No. 3 (concluding pages) - Narcotics regulation

subfiles.about: Blank UN questionnaire on limitation and control of opium poppy cultivation, raw opium production and poppy straw.
subfiles.from: United Nations
subfiles.summary: Pages are out of order. They give instructions for statistical tables, then Parts II-IV on poppy straw, control, crop substitution, and agricultural, social and economic aspects.
subfiles.title: UN Questionnaire on opium poppy and raw opium control (blank form, first copy)

subfiles.about: Japanese data for 1937-1946 on raw opium, standardized opium, exports and poppy straw use.
subfiles.from: SCAP (Japan)
subfiles.summary: Table A shows raw opium produced; remarks say it was all used for narcotic drugs and was never standardized. Tables B and C are not applicable. Table D and remarks give poppy straw use by ten companies for extract and powder, with no controls.
subfiles.title: Japan statistical Tables A-D and remarks on opium and poppy straw

subfiles.about: Japan's answers to the questionnaire (E/CN.7/63), covering poppy straw companies, prices, prohibition of cultivation and control.
subfiles.from: Crawford F. Sams, Public Health and Welfare Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Lists ten companies using poppy straw and gives prices. Poppy cultivation is prohibited by Ministry of Welfare Ordinances Nos. 46 and 25. About 200 narcotic inspectors enforce control. Opium was bought by the government at fixed prices, and farmers now grow food instead.
subfiles.title: SCAP reply to UN questionnaire on opium poppy control

subfiles.about: South Korea's answers on poppy straw, control of opium poppy, crop substitution and opium prices.
subfiles.from: Department of Public Health and Welfare, USAMGIK
subfiles.summary: Poppy cultivation is forbidden. Difficulties lie in informing remote farmers. Reports the Japanese monopoly's 1943 target, yen paid for opium 1937-43 and prices. Ordinance No. 119 and Order No. 3 are forwarded.
subfiles.title: USAMGIK reply to UN questionnaire (Korea)
subfiles.to: United Nations Commission on Narcotic Drugs

subfiles.about: English-edition Official Gazette with Finance and Welfare ordinances, chiefly the Narcotic Control Regulation (Ordinance No. 25).
subfiles.from: Japanese Government (Ministers Ishibashi and Kawai)
subfiles.summary: Finance Ordinance No. 72 on executive pay. Welfare Ordinance No. 25 is the narcotics regulation on definitions, dealer licensing, taxes, reports, records, inspection and penalties, with transitional rules. Ordinances Nos. 26 and 27 strike medicines from lists. Finance Notification No. 478 sets salary limits.
subfiles.title: Official Gazette Extra, 19 June 1946 - Japanese ministerial ordinances

subfiles.about: Second copy of the questionnaire with the Japanese statistical tables for raw opium, exports and poppy straw.
subfiles.from: United Nations
subfiles.summary: Repeats the Parts I-IV questions. Table A gives hectares and kilograms of raw opium produced, with Korean data on morphine and diacetylmorphine. Tables B and C give standardized opium production and exports. Table D is blank.
subfiles.title: UN Questionnaire on opium poppy control (second copy with Japan Tables A-D)

subfiles.about: Transmits second-quarter 1947 Statistical Forms A(GL) for Japan and Korea.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Sends Forms A(GL) on narcotics imports and exports for the second quarter of 1947, for Japan and for USAMGIK.
subfiles.title: Transmittal to President, Permanent Central Opium Board, of Statistical Form A(GL)
subfiles.to: President, Permanent Central Opium Board, Geneva

subfiles.about: Directs transmitting Japan and Korea replies to the UN Secretary-General on the drug addiction questionnaire E/CN.7/64.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Quotes a draft note enclosing the replies from Japan and USAMGIK. Refers to despatch 2290 of 30 April 1947.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 195 to U.S. Representative at UN - drug addiction questionnaire replies
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Representative to the United Nations, New York

subfiles.about: Directs transmitting replies from Japan and Korea on opium poppy control (E/CN.7/63) to the UN Secretary-General.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Gives the text of a note enclosing the Japanese and USAMGIK replies to the questionnaire.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 196 to U.S. Representative at UN - opium poppy questionnaire replies
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Representative to the United Nations, New York

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Instruction 196 and confirms the replies were sent to the UN Secretary-General.
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Representative at UN (Leroy D. Stinebower)
subfiles.summary: Confirms transmission of the Japan and Korea replies to the opium poppy questionnaire.
subfiles.title: U.S. Mission to UN despatch No. 2800 acknowledging Instruction 196

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Instruction 195 and confirms transmission of the drug addiction replies.
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Representative at UN (Leroy D. Stinebower)
subfiles.summary: Confirms the replies on drug addiction were sent to the UN Secretary-General.
subfiles.title: U.S. Mission to UN despatch No. 2801 acknowledging Instruction 195

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the State Department note of August 23, 1947 with annexes.
subfiles.from: Secretary, Permanent Central Opium Board, Geneva
subfiles.summary: Short acknowledgment of documents received.
subfiles.title: Permanent Central Opium Board acknowledgment

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Japan and Korea replies and asks for two extra copies of three Official Gazette documents.
subfiles.from: Secretary-General of the United Nations
subfiles.summary: Requests extra copies of the Japanese Gazette of 19 June 1946, USAMGIK Ordinance No. 119 and Public Health Order No. 3.
subfiles.title: UN Secretary-General note requesting extra copies of documents
subfiles.to: U.S. Representative at the Seat of the United Nations

subfiles.about: Transmits the Secretary-General's letter of 15 October 1947 acknowledging the replies and requesting extra copies.
subfiles.from: U.S. Representative at UN (Leroy D. Stinebower)
subfiles.summary: Forwards the letter of 15 October 1947 and notes the request for two additional copies of documents.
subfiles.title: U.S. Mission to UN despatch No. 4392 forwarding Secretary-General's letter

subfiles.about: Directs sending the UN Secretary-General the requested copies of the Gazette, Ordinance No. 119 and Public Health Order No. 3.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Quotes a draft note and encloses copies of the documents. Refers to despatch of 29 October 1947.
subfiles.title: Instruction to U.S. Representative at UN - transmit requested document copies
subfiles.to: U.S. Representative to the United Nations, New York

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Department's note of December 2, 1947 with enclosures.
subfiles.from: Secretary, Permanent Central Opium Board, Geneva
subfiles.summary: Short acknowledgment of documents received.
subfiles.title: Permanent Central Opium Board acknowledgment (2 December 1947)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Department's note of December 2, 1947 with annexes.
subfiles.from: Secretary, Permanent Central Opium Board, Geneva
subfiles.summary: Short acknowledgment of documents received.
subfiles.title: Permanent Central Opium Board acknowledgment (17 December 1947)

subfiles.about: Encloses SCAP's communication on third-quarter 1947 narcotics import/export reports for Japan and Korea.
subfiles.from: H. J. Anslinger, Commissioner of Narcotics
subfiles.summary: Asks transmission to the Permanent Central Opium Board. Final Statistical Forms A will follow when received.
subfiles.title: Letter from Anslinger to Morlock forwarding SCAP communication
subfiles.to: G. A. Morlock, Department of State

subfiles.about: Reports no narcotics imports or exports for Japan and Korea in the third quarter of 1947.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP (M. F. Noyes, for the Supreme Commander)
subfiles.summary: Forms A(GL) not yet received. Japan and Korea each had no imports or exports. Forms will follow.
subfiles.title: SCAP statistical report on narcotics import/export, third quarter 1947

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's report of 30 October 1947 on Japan and Korea narcotics trade.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Sends the report in duplicate. Final Forms A(GL) will follow when available.
subfiles.title: Transmittal to PCOB of SCAP third-quarter report
subfiles.to: President, Permanent Central Opium Board, Bern

subfiles.about: Routing slip stamped December 1947, file 894.114 Narcotics/12-147.
subfiles.from: U.S. Mission to the United Nations
subfiles.summary: Routing slip with stamps and file number.
